Answer: B
Reason: Figure 1a (CT) shows a hyperdense foreign body (fishbone) penetrating the esophageal wall with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating perforation. Figure 2 (CXR) demonstrates a right-sided pneumothorax (visible visceral pleural line and absent lung markings peripherally), which is a direct complication of esophageal perforation allowing air to enter the pleural space.
